title: Settings
name: Name
emailVerifyPending: We sent a confirmation link to {email}. Your email changes once you confirm it there.
emailChangeNoMail: A confirmation link is sent by email to confirm a new address, which this hub can't deliver yet — your email won't change until email is set up.
uiModeDesc: Choose how much of Tugra you see. Switch any time.
uiModeFleetDesc: Full control plane: servers, teams, deploys, monitoring.
uiModeHomeDesc: Simple launcher for your apps — the extras stay out of the way.
sessionsDesc: Sign out of every device, including this one. You'll need to sign in again.
logoutEverywhereConfirm: Sign out of all devices? Every session (including this one) will be ended and you'll need to sign in again.
passwordMin: New password must be at least 8 characters.
recoveryCodesDesc: Save these somewhere safe. Each code works once if you lose your authenticator. They won't be shown again.
sudoDesc: Confirm with your password and a current 2FA code (from your authenticator, or a recovery code).
channelsDesc: Deploy, server and SSL alerts over email, Slack, Discord and more.
apiTokensDesc: Personal access tokens for the API, the CLI and AI tools.
noTokens: Create a token to use the API, the CLI or an AI assistant.
tokenScopesHint: Every token can read. Add only what it needs.
scopeReadDesc: See servers, apps and databases. Always included.
apiAccessDesc: Control token (API/CLI) access to this instance. Your browser session is never affected.
apiEnabledHint: When off, every API token is rejected. The web app keeps working.
apiAllowedIpsHint: One IP or range per line. Leave empty to allow any address.
licenseDesc: Activate a signed license to unlock the Pro or Cloud edition. Buy one from Tugra, then paste the license token below — no restart needed.
licenseTokenHint: The signed token you received after purchase. Leave the field empty and press Remove to downgrade.
licenseNotVerified: The license was stored but did not verify
ssoDesc: Let your team sign in with your OIDC identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0, …). Accounts are created automatically on first sign-in.
ssoEnabledHint: When on, the login page offers an “Sign in with SSO” button. Requires an issuer, client ID and client secret.
ssoAllowedDomainsHint: One domain per line (e.g. company.com). New users may sign in only from these domains. Leave empty to allow any domain the provider authenticates.
updatesDesc: Track new Tugra releases and choose how they're applied.
updateOwnerApplies: The instance owner applies updates from Settings.
updaterBehindNote: The update helper runs {version}, older than this hub. The hub updates it by itself.
updaterRefreshingNote: The update helper is being refreshed to match this hub. It restarts in a few seconds.
updaterFailedNote: The update helper still runs {version}; the automatic refresh did not finish. Updates keep working. Run scripts/install.sh on the server once to refresh it.
updateAutoHint: Patch releases, and the next beta on a beta build. Minor and major versions always wait for you.
channelAutoHint: Automatic follows the running build: a beta build tracks Beta, a release build tracks Stable. Pin a channel to override.
updateChecksDisabled: Update checks are turned off for this deployment (TUGRA_UPDATE_CHECKS=0).
updateChecksEvery: Checks run every {minutes} minutes and whenever the panel is opened.
updateFailed: The update failed. Check the server logs and try again.
updateTimedOut: The new version never came up. Check the update helper's log (docker logs tugra-updater) and try again.
updateDiskShort: Not enough free disk space. The update needs about {need} free on {path}, but only {have} is available. Free some space (unused images or old backups), then click Update now again. Nothing was changed.
updateDiskFull: The disk filled up while pulling the images. Free some space, then click Update now again. Nothing was changed.
updateHalfTitle: An earlier update did not finish
updateHalfNote: This server's configuration names {envVersion} but it is still running {runningVersion}: an earlier update stopped half-way. Nothing is broken. Finish update completes it, or puts the configuration back to {runningVersion}.
updateHalfNoRelease: This server is set to {envVersion} but still runs {runningVersion}, and no newer release can finish it. Set TUGRA_VERSION={runningVersion} in .env to put it back.
updateRecoveryRequired: The update failed and the previous version could not be fully restored. Set TUGRA_VERSION to the previous version in .env and recreate hub-api and web (the server logs print the exact command).
updateInProgress: An update is already in progress.
updateUnconfigured: Automatic updates aren't configured on this instance.
updateNotifyOnly: This is a minor/major release — review the changelog, then use your installer to upgrade.
updateNeedsIntermediate: This release can't be skipped to directly — upgrade to an intermediate version first.
telemetryDesc: Share anonymous usage counts (servers, apps, deploys) with your version and OS, so we know what to build next. No IP, hostname, domain, email or names. You can turn this off anytime.
telemetryEnabledHint: Helps steer Tugra's development. Aggregate counts + version/edition/OS under a random, stable id — never names or secrets.
telemetryForcedOff: Telemetry is turned off by the server environment (TUGRA_TELEMETRY=0). Remove that variable to let this toggle take effect.
telemetrySendError: Couldn't reach the stats endpoint (that's fine — it'll retry later)
telemetryResetDone: A fresh anonymous ID was generated
telemetryThanks: Thanks — you're helping Tugra get better
sectionInstanceHint: Instance-wide settings — visible to the instance owner only.
brandingDesc: Replace the Tugra name, logo, favicon and accent color with your own, and hide the "Powered by Tugra" footer. Applies across the panel and the login page.
brandingProHint: White-label is a Pro feature. Activate a license under Plan & license to brand this instance.
brandingHidePoweredHint: Removes the Tugra attribution from the login page footer.
mail_desc: How this panel sends password-reset, verification and invite emails. Configure it here instead of editing MAIL_* environment variables.
mail_effectiveEnv: Sending through the MAIL_* environment variables (no provider selected here).
mail_effectiveNone: Email is not configured — links are written to the hub log and nothing is sent.
mail_fromHint: e.g. Tugra <no-reply@example.com>. Must be a verified sender at your provider.
mail_resendHint: Resend is sent over its SMTP relay (smtp.resend.com). Only the API key and a from address are needed.
mail_testFailedGeneric: Test email could not be sent
mail_testNeedsSave: Save your changes first — the test uses the saved settings.
hubBackup_desc: Scheduled backup of Tugra's own database (your apps, servers, settings and encrypted secrets). Runs on the local agent and is always encrypted.
hubBackup_saveFailed: Could not save the backup settings
hubBackup_envWarning: Your .env (SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY) is not in this backup. Keep it offsite; without it the backup cannot be decrypted. Destination encryption keys inside it are protected by your .env key.
hubBackup_localWarning: Stored on this same disk. Choose an S3 destination for real disaster recovery.
hubBackup_offBoxNudge: A copy on this server's own disk is lost with the server. Pick any S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Hetzner, or your own) to keep it elsewhere.
hubBackup_extraHint: Two places are good, three are safer. Every run also writes here.
hubBackup_drillDesc: Every month the newest backup is restored into a throwaway container and checked. Nothing touches your live data.
hubBackup_drillOverdue: The last drill is more than a month old.
hubBackup_deadmanDesc: The hub pings an address outside itself. If the pings stop, that service tells you the hub is down.
hubBackup_deadmanUrlSaved: Saved for {host}. Paste a new address to replace it.
hubBackup_deadmanSaveFailed: Could not save the check-in settings
hubBackup_alwaysEncrypted: Always encrypted with a key derived from your .env — this cannot be turned off.
keysExport_minLength: The passphrase must be at least 12 characters.
keysExport_warning: The file holds the decryption key of every encrypted backup destination. Treat it like your .env: keep it offline, never email it.
keysExport_done: Downloaded {name} ({count} destination key(s)). Open it with: openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -md sha256 -in <file>
keysExport_undecryptable: {count} destination key(s) could not be read and are missing from the file: {ids}
panelTlsDesc: Automatic HTTPS for this panel. Re-apply it if the certificate router needs re-provisioning.
panelTlsOff: Not configured. Set a panel domain above.
panelTlsOriginMismatch: The panel domain does not match this instance's public URL. Set the domain again above.
panelTlsEmailBad: The Let's Encrypt email is not valid, so the proxy ignores the panel. Fix it above or leave it empty.
secretsKeyDesc: Stored secrets are encrypted with data keys protected by SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Rotate the active key here without a restart; old keys stay readable until nothing uses them.
secretsKeyTotals: {current} secrets under the current key · {stale} still on an old key · {unreadable} unreadable
secretsKeyUnreadableHint: Unreadable secrets were written with a key that is no longer configured. Add that key to SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS and re-encrypt, or re-enter those values.
secretsKeyRecoveryCodes: {count} two-factor recovery codes were issued before the rotation. They keep working while the previous key is configured; users should regenerate them before it is removed.
secretsKeyRemovable: Every stored secret is under the current key — you can remove SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS from the environment and restart.
secretsKeyPending: Some secrets are still under a previous key. Keep SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS set until this card says it is safe to remove.
secretsKeyLastRun: Last run {when}: {rewritten} rewritten · {alreadyCurrent} already current · {unreadable} unreadable · {skipped} skipped · {errors} errors
secretsKeyBackupNote: A hub backup needs only the SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY that was set when it was taken. Keep an old .env key until you no longer need to restore older backups. Rotating the data key does not change SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
secretsKeyRotateBody: A new random key becomes the active key right now, with no restart and no change to your .env file. Existing secrets stay readable under their old keys.
secretsKeyRotateStale: The active key changed while this page was open. The list was refreshed; check it and try again.

secretsKeyErr.referenced: Stored secrets still use this key. Re-encrypt first.
secretsKeyErr.grace: This key was replaced moments ago. Wait a minute, then retire it.
secretsKeyErr.rotation_running: A re-encryption is running. Wait for it to finish.
secretsKeyErr.ring_degraded: A data key cannot be unwrapped with the configured .env key, so changes are blocked.
secretsKeyErr.no_root: No configured .env key can unwrap this key. Put the old key back in SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS.
secretsKeyErr.not_decrypt_only: Only a decrypt-only key can be retired.
secretsKeyErr.not_retired: Only a retired key can be restored.
secretsKeyErr.already_env_root: The .env key is already the encryption key.
secretsKeyErr.stale_current: The active key changed. Reload and try again.
secretsKeyErr.unknown_key: That key is not managed here.

secretsKeyBlocked.grace: Replaced moments ago, wait a minute

secretsKeyDegraded: The key ring is degraded: {reason}. Fix SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or set the previous key in SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS) and restart. Rotation is disabled meanwhile.
secretsKeyDowngradeNote: Some secrets are stored under a rotated key. Before rolling back to an older Tugra release, switch back to the .env key and let the re-encryption finish.
secretsKeyBackToEnvConfirm: Make the SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY from your .env the encryption key again and re-encrypt all secrets under it? Rotated keys stay readable until you retire them.
appearanceDesc: How Tugra looks on this device. Stored in your browser only — nothing is sent to the server.
appearanceThemeHint: Light, dark, follow your system, or build your own.
appearanceScaleHint: Make everything a little smaller to fit more on screen. Phones always use 100%.
appearanceWidthHint: Let pages use the full window, or keep them in a centered column on wide screens.
appearanceNavHint: The sidebar either runs edge to edge or floats as a framed panel on a dotted background.
appearanceStyleHint: Flat is the standard look. 3D gives cards a raised edge that lifts on hover.
appearanceChartTimesHint: Chart tooltips and deployment timestamps show your local time, optionally with the same moment in UTC.
tokenRotateBody: A new secret is issued for "{name}" and the current one stops working immediately. Update every script or CI job that uses it.
updateReloadHint: This page is still running the old version until you reload.
panelDomain_desc: Where this panel lives. Point a DNS record at this server, enter the domain, and Tugra sets up free HTTPS.
panelDomain_modeIp: Open at {url} (plain http, through Tugra's own proxy on port 80). Add a domain below to switch to https.
panelDomain_modeDomain: Served at {url} with an automatic certificate.
panelDomain_modePort: Published on a raw port ({url}). Setting a domain also needs ports 80 and 443 free on this server.
panelDomain_invalid: Enter a bare hostname such as panel.example.com (no https://, path or port).
panelDomain_dnsHint: Point the domain's A record at this server first.
panelDomain_removeConfirm: Go back to http://<server-ip>/? {domain} stops working and you sign in again.
panelDomain_removeNeedsIp: The hub doesn't know this server's public IP. Enter it to continue.
panelDomain_serverOffline: The local server is offline. Bring it online to change the panel domain.
panelDomain_startFailed: Couldn't start the panel domain change
panelDomain_stepCertificate: Waiting for the Let's Encrypt certificate
panelDomain_stepSwitching: Switching the panel address and restarting the hub
panelDomain_switchingNote: The panel is moving to {url}. This page stops responding at the old address in a moment — open the new one and sign in again.
panelDomain_doneNote: The panel now lives at {url}. Agents on other servers are moved to it automatically; the previous address keeps answering them until they have.
panelDomain_failed: The change did not go through.
panelDomain_fail_cert_timeout: The certificate was not issued in time. Your previous address still works and nothing else was touched. Check the DNS record and that port 80 is open. Behind Cloudflare, SSL/TLS mode must be Full and Always Use HTTPS off.
panelDomain_fail_proxy_failed: The proxy couldn't be configured: {error}. Your previous address still works.
panelDomain_fail_updater_stale: The update helper didn't pick the change up. Your previous address still works. Update the helper first (Settings → Updates), then try again.
panelDomain_fail_updater_failed: The hub couldn't switch to the new address: {error}
panelDomain_fail_unreachable: The new address got a certificate but did not answer, so the change was reverted and your previous address works again: {error}. Behind Cloudflare, set SSL/TLS mode to Full (not Flexible) and turn Always Use HTTPS off.
panelDomain_fail_restore_unverified: The hub could not switch to the new address and the previous setup could not be confirmed healthy: {error}. Check the server (docker compose ps in the install directory) before trying again.
panelDomain_fail_interrupted: The change was interrupted before the address was switched. Your previous address still works. Try again.
panelDomain_agentsProgress: {moved} of {total} agents moved to the new address.
panelDomain_agentsSwitching: Agents are already being pointed at the new address; the panel switches in a moment.
panelDomain_agentReason_offline: offline — it moves when it reconnects
panelDomain_agentReason_old_agent: agent too old to follow — update it (Servers → Update agent)
panelDomain_agentsKept: The previous address keeps answering agents until all have moved, you stop waiting, or {date} at the latest. Nothing is lost in the meantime.
panelDomain_agentsReleaseConfirm: Stop answering the previous address for the agents that have not moved? Those agents lose the hub until they are re-installed with a fresh install command.
panelDomain_agentsReleased: Stopped waiting for the remaining agents
recoveryAckHint: Copy, download or print them first.
recoveryFileHint: Each code works once. Keep this file somewhere safe.
scanHint: Scan this with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code.
signOutOthersBody: Every other session ends. This device stays signed in.
signOutOthersFailed: Couldn't sign out the other sessions.
require2faDesc: Owners and admins without two-factor are sent to set it up before they can do anything else.
require2faNeedsOwn: Turn on 2FA for your own account first.
uiModeConfirmBodyServers: You have {servers}. Home mode shows only this machine and hides the Servers page.
uiModeConfirmBodyTeams: You have {servers} and {teams}. Home mode shows only this machine and hides the Servers page and team views.
uiModeConfirmBodyUnknown: Home mode shows only this machine and hides the Servers page and team views.
tokenMcpHint: Read-only. Lets an AI assistant look at your servers and apps, never change them.
tokenExpiryNeverHint: A token that never expires works until you revoke it.
tokenRevealHint: This is the only time it's shown.
tokenCloseBody: This token won't be shown again. If you haven't saved it, you'll have to create a new one.
tokenMcpCommandHint: Run this in your terminal. It includes the token.
tokenMcpCommandLabel: Command to add this hub to Claude Code
tokenUsageNote: The last 50 calls. The token itself is never stored.
apiOffNotice: API access is off: tokens will not work right now.
tokenOnce: Copy this token now — it won't be shown again.
panelDomain_cloudflare: Behind Cloudflare? Keep SSL/TLS on Full (not Flexible) while the first certificate is issued.
hubHealthHint: How this hub itself is doing. Sampled every 20 s in memory; nothing is written to the database.
hubHealthRestartsHint: Process starts in the last 24 hours, from the recorded boot times.
hubWarn_heap_high: Heap is at {value}% of its limit (warns at {limit}%).
hubWarn_loop_lag: Event loop p99 is {value} ms (warns at {limit} ms).
hubWarn_pg_connections: Postgres connections are at {value}% of the maximum.
hubWarn_redis_memory: Redis is at {value}% of its memory limit.
hubWarn_restarts: The hub restarted {value} times in the last 24 hours.
